name: route-on-confirm-by-document-type
summary: Native rule on the intake queue: on annotation_confirmed (automated or human), change_queue to the destination for the listed document types, always with reimport: true. One rule per destination.

rule_name.description: rule name, max 255 characters; name the destination role, e.g. 'Inbox - route invoices and credit notes to <destination>'

inbox_queue_url.description: URL of the intake (inbox) queue the rule is attached to

document_type_field.description: schema id of the document-type enum field; the same value in all three routing parts

document_types.description: the types this destination takes, as comma-separated single-quoted Python literals, e.g. 'tax_invoice', 'credit_note'; each must be an option of the enum

destination_queue_url.description: URL of the queue the document moves to

provenance: Lifted from a production deployment of a classic intake (test 2026-11-12/13, production 2026-11-16): one rule per destination on the inbox. Both paths verified live: an automated confirm and a human confirm after review each moved the document and ran the destination's initialize hooks. reimport: true was chosen after reimport: false was measured skipping the destination's initialize chain and carrying the source queue's automation blockers; a second, independent SA reported the same. Senior-SA sign-off for standard: JŠ (2026-11-25).
notes: Always reimport: true into a destination; the one exception is a return trip whose content must survive, and only while the target runs automation never. Keep the intake queue on use_confirmed_state: true (a historic reimport skip, 6 of 19 moves, was tied to use_confirmed_state: false on the source). Without the Record and Restore parts, a re-import re-predicts the type and a person's correction on the inbox is lost. A plain manual move fires no initialize, so nothing is restored on it.
